translation: Target defines the proposition (Prop) asserting that the falsum formula fls is not derivable from the empty set of hypotheses ∅ in the deductive system Def14 (that is, ¬ Def14 ∅ fls, expressing the consistency of the pure proof system with no additional premises). Here formulas (Form) are built from binary atomic formulas atom r x y (with natural-number relation index r and natural-number variable arguments x, y), falsum fls, implication imp, universal quantification all x over natural-number variables, and a unary modal operator K. Derivability from a set of formulas T (Def14 T) is defined inductively as the smallest set of formulas containing every axiom in Def13 and every hypothesis in T (which contributes nothing when T = ∅) and closed under modus ponens (from imp φ ψ and φ, derive ψ); neither universal generalization nor necessitation is an inference rule of Def14. The axiom set Def13 consists of all formulas in Def12 together with all formulas of the form K ψ where ψ is in Def12. The set Def12 is the closure of the base axioms Def11 under applying universal quantification all x zero or more times. The base axioms Def11 consist of: (1) all propositional tautologies (Def10: formulas φ such that v φ holds for every v : Form → Prop satisfying ¬ v fls and v (imp ψ χ) ↔ (v ψ → v χ) for all ψ, χ); (2) universal instantiation imp (all x φ) (Def7 x y φ), replacing free occurrences of x by y, subject to the side condition Def8 y x φ that y is free for x in φ (no free occurrence of x lies within the scope of an all y binder); (3) universal distribution imp (all x (imp φ ψ)) (imp (all x φ) (all x ψ)); (4) vacuous quantification imp φ (all x φ) whenever x does not occur free in φ (¬ Def6 x φ); (5) modal distribution imp (K (imp φ ψ)) (imp (K φ) (K ψ)); (6) imp (K φ) φ; (7) imp (K φ) (K (K φ)); and (8) imp (K (all x φ)) (all x (K φ)). Target takes no parameters or hypotheses, merely defines this proposition without proving it, and does not reference Def15, Def16, Def17, or the derived connectives neg, and, iff, ex.
